ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an oxygen-containing heterocyclic-style transition-state structure, with an O atom on the left, the top carbon connected to NMe2, an alkene part containing R1 on the right, and the lower-left carbon connected to R. There are also several curved arrows and a right-side arrow trajectory in the figure; they represent electron transfer or a reaction path, not actual chemical bonds. Reasoning count: Count the actual bond connections between non-hydrogen atoms one by one, not counting arrows. The countable bonds are: 1 O–top C, 1 O–lower-left C, 1 top C–N, 2 N–Me bonds, 1 top C=C right-side connection, 1 lower-left C–R, 1 lower-left C–lower alkene C, 1 lower alkene C=C connection to the carbon bearing R1, and 1 carbon bearing R1–R1. Total 1+1+1+2+1+1+1+1+1 = 10.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the image and separate real bond lines from reaction arrows. Count the non-hydrogen bond connections one by one: O–C(top), O–C(lower-left), C(top)–N, two N–Me bonds, C(top)=C(right), C(lower-left)–R, C(lower-left)–C(lower alkene), C(lower alkene)=C(R1-bearing carbon), and C(R1-bearing carbon)–R1. Do not count any curved arrow or the apparent right-side arrow path as a bond. The tally gives 10.

method.method_draft: Construct an adjacency list from the drawing: O is adjacent to C(top) and C(lower-left); C(top) is adjacent to O, N, and the right alkene carbon; N is adjacent to C(top), Me, and Me; C(lower-left) is adjacent to O, R, and the lower alkene carbon; the lower alkene carbon is adjacent to the R1-bearing carbon; the R1-bearing carbon is adjacent to R1.
